Subject: Eval governance handoff and exception path for promptset A/B

Team —

Quick note to align on a lightweight governance path for Tilt's upcoming A/B on promptset A. They want to run against our hosted inference with the new promptset_v2; their QA flagged a potential quality delta that could block launch if we treat it as a hard failure. We should agree what constitutes an "exception" vs. a hard rollback.

Asks:
- Marissa: propose the acceptance checklist and stoplight thresholds (precision/recall/qualitative failures).
- Karthik: confirm whether we can run an isolated canary on dedicated capacity and what latency/throughput differences to expect.
- Dev: capture any infra/obs gaps (tracing, sample retention) we need to satisfy audit for the exception flow.

Attachments: draft promptset_A_v2.csv (sample prompts) and regression-matrix-tilt-0427.xlsx (initial failure modes).

Goal: have a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) + exception path by EOD tomorrow so Tilt can proceed with the scheduled A/B on Wednesday.

Thanks —

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the quick sync. Two clarifications from our side:

1) The QA team found a 6% regression on our task-level accuracy for one taxonomy (billing-related clarifications). That was flagged against the primary promptset baseline, not the control.
2) We want the ability to continue the A/B if regressions fall within the "managed-exception" boundaries you propose. Stopping mid-run will be costly for our testing cadence.

I attached a short note with the failing examples we saw (I'll upload to the Drive link as well). Happy to jump on a quick call Monday morning if helpful.

Subject: Re: Eval governance handoff and exception path for promptset A/B

Quick proposal attached (ma_plan_draft_0427.md). Summary here:

- Acceptance thresholds (primary): task accuracy >= baseline - 3 percentage points for core taxonomies; precision drop <= 5% for NLU labels.
- Exception window: regressions that (a) are taxonomy-limited, (b) have reproducible counterexamples >= 5 shards, and (c) no PII/exfiltration signal.
- Operational mitigation during exception: run extended logging (3x samples), enable prefix cache bypass for affected routes, and schedule daily triage for 72 hours.

Stop criteria (hard rollback): any regression impacting payments/consent flows, or any spike in hallucination rate > 8% in audited sample.

Next steps: if we agree, I'll convert the doc to a MAP and send to Tilt for sign-off.

Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Eval Acceptance
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Eval governance handoff and exception path for promptset A/B

Couple of technical clarifications on Marissa's proposal:

- Canary option: we can run the A/B on a dedicated small pool (2x T4-equivalent) with identical model weights; throughput will be ~70% of prod without batching. Latency delta ~20ms median. We can enable a routing policy to send 10% of Tilt traffic there.
- Observability: we need the extended logging toggle implemented — Dev, can you confirm ETA to add a flag that increases sample retention (from 1k/day -> 5k/day) and prevents token-stripping?
- KV cache: if we bypass prefix cache for affected routes we must be explicit about token-cost increase and shared-customer impact. Recommend bounding the bypass to the test route only.

If those are fine, engineering can stand up the canary by Tuesday evening PST.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Tue 10:30am PT to confirm MAP updates and canary readiness.
